lessons.title: Pushes, pulls and motion
lessons.description: Describe how a force can change an object's movement or shape.
lessons.content: A force is a push or pull. Forces can start or stop motion, change an object's speed or direction, or change its shape. A force may act through contact or at a distance, such as gravity attracting objects towards Earth.
learning_objectives: Identify pushes and pulls in familiar activities.
Describe possible effects of a force on an object.
prerequisites: Observe moving and stationary objects safely.

explanation_sections.title: Effects of a force
explanation_sections.body: Kicking a stationary ball can set it moving. A hand can slow a rolling toy. Squeezing a soft object can change its shape. These examples show different effects; the result depends on the object and the forces acting on it.

explanation_sections.title: Balanced and unbalanced situations
explanation_sections.body: When forces on an object are balanced, its motion does not change. An unbalanced force can change its motion. Recap: describe the object before and after the force to explain its effect.

worked_examples.prompt: A moving toy car slows when it rolls over a rough mat. What force interaction helps explain the change?
worked_examples.solution: Friction between the car and mat opposes the motion.
worked_examples.reasoning: Friction acts between touching surfaces and can slow moving objects.

lessons.author: ElimuQuest Curriculum Team

questions.explanation: A pull brings an object towards the person applying the force.

questions.prompt: Which is a possible effect of an unbalanced force?
options: A change in speed or direction
An object gaining a new name
A change in colour every time
questions.correct_answer: A change in speed or direction
questions.explanation: An unbalanced force can change an object's motion.

questions.prompt: Why may a rolling ball slow down on grass?
options: Friction between the ball and grass opposes its motion.
The ball has no mass on grass.
The grass pushes it forward without contact.
questions.correct_answer: Friction between the ball and grass opposes its motion.
questions.explanation: Friction between contacting surfaces can oppose motion and slow the ball.

lessons.title: Energy changes in everyday devices
lessons.description: Trace useful energy changes in familiar appliances without saying energy disappears.
lessons.content: Energy can be transferred and changed from one form to another. A lamp transfers electrical energy mainly into light and thermal energy. A device may also transfer energy to its surroundings as sound or unwanted heating.
learning_objectives: Name common forms of energy in everyday examples.
Describe a useful energy change in a familiar device.
prerequisites: Recognise simple household devices and their purposes.

explanation_sections.title: Energy stores and transfers
explanation_sections.body: A battery stores chemical energy that can be transferred electrically in a circuit. A lamp then transfers energy to light and thermal surroundings. The main useful output depends on the device's purpose.

explanation_sections.title: Follow the transfer
explanation_sections.body: Describe the starting energy and the useful and less useful outputs. Energy is transferred, not destroyed. Recap: for each device, ask what goes in, what useful change occurs, and where other energy is transferred.

worked_examples.prompt: Describe the main useful energy change in a torch when switched on.
worked_examples.solution: Chemical energy in the battery is transferred electrically and becomes light energy, with some thermal energy.
worked_examples.reasoning: The torch's purpose is to provide light; warming is also an output.

lessons.author: ElimuQuest Curriculum Team

questions.prompt: What is the main useful output of an electric lamp?
questions.explanation: A lamp is designed mainly to produce light, though it may also warm its surroundings.

questions.prompt: What happens to energy when an appliance becomes warm?
options: Energy has been transferred into thermal energy.
questions.correct_answer: Energy has been transferred into thermal energy.
questions.explanation: Warming is evidence that energy was transferred to thermal energy in the appliance or surroundings.

questions.prompt: Which energy store is present in a charged cell before it powers a torch?
questions.explanation: A cell stores chemical energy that can be transferred in an electric circuit.
